column2: qeth currently tracks the index of the buffer that it

column1: expects to complete the next IO on each qeth_channel. If the channel
presents an IRQ while this buffer has not yet completed
processing for _any_ completed buffer takes place.
So if the 'next buffer' is skipped for any sort of reason* (eg. when it
is released due to error conditions
buffer obviously won't switch to PROCESSED until it is eventually
allocated for a _different_ IO and completes.

column2: all completion processing on that channel stalls

column1: and pending requests possibly time out.

column2: remove the whole 'next buffer' logic and simply process any

column1: IO buffer right when it completes. A channel will never have more than

column2: so there's no risk of processing out-of-sequence.
